summary: No held thesis is broken by evidence in the files. Today's three fills were MCO (buy), VTI (buy) and BND (sale). MCO was on the menu and its stored case quotes my morning numbers correctly: F-score 8/9, CFO $2.90B against net income $2.46B, and the Industrials SIC label read as Financials by bucket. It was not in my top ten, though; its gp_sector_pct of 0.826 is below every name I ranked, and the PM bought it for the Market Analyst's Financials tilt, not for fundamental rank. The day's moves (equity -$2.46; VRSN -1.47%, EXEL -2.75%, DPZ +1.37%, CARG +1.44%) are one session of price and grade nothing. No lesson in learning.json names this role and I have no graded calls, so none shaped this review. L3 and L6 (written for the proposer and PM) shaped the notes on MCO's label and its stop text.
update: Held names, from my files only. (1) MCO: the fundamentals still hold (cash flow above earnings, F8). My morning flag on the shared Industrials mislabel and the failed leverage_not_up test applies to both MCO and MSCI. Since the 11-16 decision treats them as one financial-data sleeve, the leverage failure is a sleeve-level concern too. Its stored text has an L6 mismatch: the invalidation says 'more than 8% below its recorded average fill', but the stop is a fixed $470 that the PM calls a placeholder. The next run should restate it as a dollar stop measured from the $509.04 fill. (2) EXEL closed 3.2% above its $65 stop after -2.75% today. That is price, not a thesis break; the fundamentals (F7, gp_sector_pct 0.935, CFO above net income) are unchanged. (3) INCY's 11-13 MAESTRA-3 cancellation is a pipeline item with guidance kept and does not touch the annual figures I argue from. (4) WMT: the 8-K 5.02 filed 11-16 is unread three sessions before the 11-19 print. It is a governance item, not an accounting one (no 4.01 or 4.02), but it needs reading before any WMT decision. (5) VRSN, DPZ, CARG, IDXX, FAST, KR and MSCI: nothing new in the files. KR's cyber item is still unconfirmed. (6) BND was sold; it was never screenable, so I have no fundamental view on the exit. (7) VOO and VTI are index funds outside the screen. Today's VTI add was a market-regime call, not one I can judge on fundamentals. Data caveat for tomorrow: the menu is dated 11-10 and the annual figures predate most Q3 prints. The 'screen drops X from the menu' clauses in the EXEL and MCO theses only work if the menu refreshes. If it stays dated 11-10, those clauses cannot trip, and the PM should know that.
